prompt:
Write the router for this single-page app: matching, typed params, specificity, reverse links
and construction-time conflict detection.

Already in the workspace:
  src/query.js            the app's ONE definition of query-string handling. Read its header.
                          Do not edit it and do not write a second copy of those rules - require it.
  routes.config.json      the nested route table the app ships with.
  src/nav.js              the top nav. hrefFor() hardcodes its URLs and two of them are wrong.
  tests/router.spec.js    the contract. It fails now. Do not edit it.
  public/index.html       the page shell.

Run `node tests/router.spec.js` to see what is missing; it must end up passing unmodified.

Write src/router.js, CommonJS, ending in `module.exports = { createRouter };`.

createRouter(routes) takes an array of nodes { path, name, children? }. A node's full path is its
own path appended to its ancestors'. Only LEAF nodes - nodes with no children - can be matched.

PATHS. Split a path on '/' and drop every empty segment, so leading, trailing and doubled slashes
never matter ('#/users//' is '#/users'). A segment is one of:
  literal        matches that exact segment, compared against the RAW, still-encoded text,
                 case-sensitive
  :name          captures exactly one segment
  :name<c>       captures one segment only when the DECODED value matches constraint c
  :name?         optional, allowed only as the last segment: captures one segment or none
  :name<c>?      both: optional, and constrained when it is present
  *name          captures all remaining segments, possibly none
There are exactly three constraints, and any other name makes createRouter throw
`new Error('unknown constraint: ' + c)`:
  int    /^-?[0-9]+$/
  slug   /^[a-z0-9]+(?:-[a-z0-9]+)*$/
  uuid   /^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}$/
Captured values are decoded with decodeURIComponent AFTER the split, so '%2F' stays inside one
param value and a literal '+' in a path segment stays a plus (the '+ means space' rule belongs to
query strings, not paths). A *name value is each remaining segment decoded, then joined with '/'.
params keys appear in the order their placeholders appear in the path; an optional param that
captured nothing is simply not a key.

resolve(hash) -> an object with exactly the keys { name, params, query, chain }.
  A leading '#' is optional, and '', '#', '#/' and '/' all mean '/'. Everything after the first
  '?' is the query string and is parsed with parseQuery from src/query.js. chain is the names from
  the outermost ancestor down to the matched leaf. With no match, return
  { name: 'not-found', params: {}, query: <still parsed>, chain: ['not-found'] }.

SPECIFICITY decides which leaf wins, never declaration order. Score each segment of a pattern:
literal 4, a constrained param 3, a plain param 2, '*name' 1. Compare two candidates' score arrays
element by element, larger wins; if one array is a prefix of the other, the pattern with FEWER
segments wins.

CONFLICTS are a construction-time error. Normalise every leaf's full path by replacing ':name'
with ':', ':name<c>' with ':<c>', and appending '?' for an optional one, and '*name' with '*'.
If two leaves normalise to the same string, createRouter must throw
`new Error('ambiguous routes: ' + first + ' and ' + second)` naming the first two such leaves in
depth-first declaration order.

link(name, params, query) builds a hash for a named leaf.
  Unknown name -> throw `new Error('unknown route: ' + name)`.
  A required ':name' whose value is undefined, null or '' -> throw
    `new Error('missing param: ' + name)`.
  A value that is present but breaks its constraint -> throw `new Error('invalid param: ' + name)`.
  Each captured value is encoded with encodeURIComponent, so a '/' inside a param becomes %2F;
  a '*name' value is split on '/' and each piece encoded separately, then rejoined with '/', and
  an empty wildcard adds no segment; an optional param that is undefined, null or '' adds no
  segment. The result starts with '#/', and the query from stringifyQuery is appended after a '?'
  only when that string is non-empty. resolve(link(n, p, q)) must give back name n and params p.

Finally, in src/nav.js replace the body of hrefFor() so every href comes from router.link().
Leave renderNav()'s markup and the LINKS table exactly as they are, and keep the module's exports.

checks.regex: two leaves with the same pattern are rejected at construction

checks.contains: files{rest=a/b/c/d/e} not-found{} not-found{} tag-raw{raw=a+b} tag-raw{raw=a+b} not-found{} not-found{} user-overview{id=007} q={"a":"1?b=2"}
p3 p1 p2 u1 not-found [invalid param: a] [ambiguous routes: n1 and n2]

checks.cmd: node -e 'var s=require("fs").readFileSync("./src/router.js","utf8");if(!/require\((.)\.\/query\.js\1\)/.test(s)){console.error("router must require ./query.js");process.exit(1);}if(/split\((.)&\1\)/.test(s)){console.error("router must not parse the query itself");process.exit(1);}console.log("ok");'
